headline: Computational inference of RNA from sequence, raw current, and mass spectra
label: Computational Rna Design And Analysis
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply deep learning and spectral methods to RNA therapeutic design and direct molecular measurement.
synthesis: The common thread is computational inference on RNA molecules directly from sequence, raw signal, or spectra, aimed at either therapeutic design or molecular measurement. DeepRNAi predicts on- and off-target siRNA knockdown from siRNA and mRNA sequence and releases a training and benchmark dataset. A nanopore approach classifies E. coli tRNA species from direct RNA ionic currents without basecalling, reporting 98.2% accuracy. OligoFragger uses spectrum graphs to constrain modified-oligonucleotide MS/MS searches with FDR control. BIOREDIS integrates nine resources for end-to-end design of RNA and DNA therapeutics, including codon optimization and shRNA/siRNA design. The new contributions are benchmarking, signal-level classification, spectrum-guided search and workflow integration; the items do not report head-to-head comparisons across these tools.
